_note: SWITCHED-OFF HOOKS. Nothing here runs. Claude Code never reads this file; it
reads ../settings.json only. This is the parking bay, and every entry below is
in the exact shape it takes inside that file's `hooks` object, so turning one on
is a move, not a rewrite.
They used to be parked inside settings.json under a "//" key. That stopped
working: Claude Code validates hook event names now, and a "//" holding
PreToolUse entries makes it discard the entire settings file - permissions and
all - with only a toast to say so. JSON still has no comment syntax, and an
unknown key inside `hooks` is no longer a safe place to hide one, so the
To turn one on: copy its object into `hooks` in ../settings.json under the same
event name, and drop its _why - the reason belongs beside the wiring. If that
event already has entries, append to the array; every hook on an event runs, in
parallel. The code is in this folder, and `node .claude/hooks/selftest.mjs`
proves each one still runs and decides.

_why: THE TIMELINE, BEFORE THE TURN ENDS. 'Every session, ask whether anything
belongs on it, and add it before you close.' An event that never reaches the
timeline has no route back: the spine is what makes a detail findable in one
read a year later. If anything under data/ moved today and timeline.md did not,
this refuses the end of the turn once, listing what was written. Once per
session, never twice - a second refusal is an argument, and she is waiting on
the other side of it.
NOT SAFE TO WIRE AS IT STANDS (SAF-005, 'After a crisis, the person comes
before the record.'): this hook checks for no crisis marker, so it would ask
for filing in the middle of a crisis. crisis-floor.mjs now writes one (a
'YYYY-MM-DD · crisis · ongoing' line in the core session log, read through
lib/opening.mjs); have this stand down on it for that session and the next.
THE RECORD'S OWN CHECKS, EARLY. ux/ already owns three: the crisis numbers
still parse (SAF-02), nothing personal reached a harness file (HAR-02), nothing
in the record points at a file that no longer exists. They run at build - days
later, on a different machine, for whoever is deploying. Their whole value is
being early, so this runs them at the end of any turn that touched data/ or ux/
and blocks on failure with the real output. Ordinary conversation pays nothing.
Order note: hooks on one event run in parallel, so this and save-record both
start - deliberate. Saving must never wait on a lint.
NOT SAFE TO WIRE AS IT STANDS (SAF-005): it blocks the end of a turn, and
does not yet read the crisis marker crisis-floor.mjs writes (see
timeline-before-close above). It must stand down on it first.
THE SESSION COUNT THE TRIGGERS RUN ON. data/core/state/log.md is 'One line per
session, and maintenance triggers' - upkeep at 8 sessions, review at 25,
research at 30. Every one of those thresholds is counted in session lines, so a
session that ends without one makes all three quietly wrong, and the thresholds
are what stop the record rotting. This writes only the shape - date, session,
files touched - for the sessions that end without a goodbye; the playbook and
the one clause stay the model's to write while it still knows what happened.
